newsitem.title: USA: Christopher successor said to need broader mandate.
newsitem.headline: Christopher successor said to need broader mandate.

text.p: President Bill Clinton must pay far more attention to foreign policy in his second term and give a broader mandate to his new secretary of state, a leading Senate foreign policy expert said on Friday.

Sen. Richard Lugar, R-Indiana, a senior member of the Foreign Relations Committee, ruled himself out as a possible secretary of state and questioned whether U.S. policy would benefit from the choice of a Republican to fill the job.

Lugar's name has been mentioned as a possible choice as secretary of state to succeed Warren Christopher, whose resignation was announced on Thursday, on the theory that it would help to achieve a more bipartisan foreign policy.

"I am not certain there is any benefit in that," Lugar told a news conference. He said the new foreign policy chief "had better forge a new contract with President Clinton" with more latitude than Christopher had to deal with foreign policy issues.

Lugar called for a "fundamental re-examination" of foreign policy by the administration and Congress. He said the first indication of Clinton's foreign policy priorities would be whether he pushed for more money from Congress to run the foreign affairs establishment. Christopher complained that State Department funding was cut to a dangerously low level.
"The president must join us in this advocacy and devote a much larger share of his personal attention to foreign policy during his second term," Lugar said.

He said the new secretary of state should have a broad mandate and flexibility to pursue solutions to foreign policy problems and could not "be involved in helping to win the election of the year 2000 for the Democratic Party."

Lugar said the most immediate problems facing the new administration would be the future of U.S. involvement in Bosnia and the restructuring of the NATO alliance. He said the long-term foreign policy priorities were relations with China and Asian security issues.
